title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Payment of Litigation Costs in Cases Where State-Owned Financial Asset Management Companies Dispose of Non-Performing Assets of State-Owned Commercial Banks
keywords_en: non-performing asset cases of state-owned commercial banks
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Litigation Fees for Cases Involving State-Owned Financial Asset Management Companies' Disposal of Non-Performing Assets of State-Owned Commercial Banks

Fa [2001] No. 156

All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Recently, people's courts at various levels have successively accepted, in accordance with the law, a number of cases involving the disposal of non-performing assets stripped from state-owned commercial banks by the four state-owned financial asset management companies, namely, Huarong, Great Wall, Cinda, and Orient. According to relevant departments of the State Council, such cases concerning the four state-owned asset management companies are numerous in quantity and involve large subject matters, and the required litigation fees are also substantial, and it has been requested that appropriate reductions or exemptions be granted. In order to support the reform of the national financial system, prevent the loss of state-owned assets, alleviate the fee burden on asset management companies in the process of disposing of non-performing assets of state-owned commercial banks, and enable the prompt lawful disposal of such non-performing assets, notice is hereby given on the issues of litigation fees to be paid in the trial of such cases as follows:

1. For any case in which the aforementioned financial asset management company initiates litigation (including appeals and applications for enforcement) for the purpose of disposing of non-performing assets of state-owned commercial banks, the case acceptance fee, enforcement application fee, and preservation application fee shall be calculated in accordance with the provisions of the Measures on Litigation Fees Charged by People's Courts and shall be reduced by half.

2. In the aforementioned cases, where a financial asset management company applies for property preservation, it shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Article 5 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Assets Formed by Non-performing Loans of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies (Fa Shi [2001] No. 12).

3. With respect to litigation fees actually incurred in the course of litigation, as well as expenses such as travel expenses that should be collected from the parties in accordance with the provisions of the Supplementary Provisions to the Measures on Litigation Fees Charged by People's Courts, people's courts at all levels shall strictly collect fees according to the items and amounts actually incurred.

4. People's courts at all levels shall strictly implement the above provisions and shall not arbitrarily raise the fee collection standards, change the fee calculation methods, or collect other fees such as litigation activity fees or enforcement activity fees in violation of the provisions.

5. The matters stipulated in this notice shall be implemented from the date of issuance and shall be abrogated on February 28, 2006. For cases already accepted prior to the issuance of this notice, the litigation fees collected shall not be refunded. If a people's court has previously decided to allow a party to defer payment in handling such cases, the portion exceeding the limit specified in this notice shall no longer be recovered.

October 25, 2001
